bug_semantics: The Zalo webhook router matched a registered route using the normalized URL pathname, but unauthenticated failure accounting used the raw req.url, including its query string, as part of the key in a process-global Map with no maximum size or expiry. An attacker could repeatedly POST to the same reachable valid webhook path with an invalid or missing secret while varying ?nonce=..., causing every 401 to create and retain a distinct webhookStatusCounters entry and eventually exert memory pressure or trigger OOM. The similarly raw-URL-keyed rate-limit map was also unbounded, although that path ran only after successful target authentication; the unauthenticated advisory path is the 401 status-counter insertion.
flaw_origin: Commit a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3 added Zalo webhook ingress hardening, including anomaly accounting and rate limiting. In extensions/zalo/src/monitor.ts it introduced webhookStatusCounters as an unbounded Map, recordWebhookStatus() as an unconditional insertion for security error statuses, and calls that passed req.url for pre-authentication 401 responses. This composed a normalized route match with attacker-controlled raw-URL keying and unbounded retention; later commit 453664f09d0911cc1829d22c63f664f0ad2c8c10 only moved the already-vulnerable logic into monitor.webhook.ts.
ai_marker: absent — git cat-file -p a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3 shows human author and committer Peter Steinberger <steipete@gmail.com>, subject 'fix(security): harden feishu and zalo webhook ingress', no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, no other trailer, and no bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/security/advisories/GHSA-wr6m-jg37-68xh states that unauthenticated query-string churn on one valid Zalo webhook route caused unbounded in-memory key growth, with affected versions <= 2026.2.26 and patched versions >= 2026.3.1; the assigned API bundle expresses the package range as < 2026.3.1 and first patched version 2026.3.1.

At a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3, src/plugin-sdk/webhook-targets.ts:28-40 parses req.url and matches only normalizeWebhookPath(url.pathname), proving that distinct query strings reach the same registered route. In extensions/zalo/src/monitor.ts, the BIC adds the unbounded webhookStatusCounters Map at line 95, derives status keys as `${path}:${statusCode}` and inserts them at lines 169-171, and passes raw req.url on unauthenticated/ambiguous 401 paths at lines 202 and 208. It also uses raw req.url for the post-authentication rate-limit key at lines 212-216.

numactl-prefixed git log -L 225,241:extensions/zalo/src/monitor.ts at 58309fd8d90d69e48754ce8795218dab4c129f27 resolves recordWebhookStatus() to a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3. git log --all -SwebhookStatusCounters shows a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3 as the original addition, 453664f09d0911cc1829d22c63f664f0ad2c8c10 as the later file split/move, and 43cad8268d46a3663c79be831f2cacb015114882 as the corrective replacement; blame was used only to select and verify the exact lines.

Direct parent-tree verification: git grep -n -E 'webhookStatusCounters|recordWebhookStatus|rateLimitKey|req\.url.*statusCode' e0aaf2d399753e0a80d73409f30567394ee4a8b5 -- extensions/zalo/src/monitor.ts returned no matches. The parent handler still returned 401 for invalid/ambiguous secrets but had no status-counter insertion or raw-URL-keyed rate-limit state. The a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3 diff directly adds all parts of the flawed mechanism, so the immediate parent lacks it.

Fix commit 43cad8268d46a3663c79be831f2cacb015114882 changes extensions/zalo/src/monitor.webhook.ts to use the matched resolver path for 401 accounting (lines 138, 151, 157), replaces the counter with createBoundedCounter(maxTrackedKeys=4096, ttlMs=6 hours) at lines 55-58, replaces the rate-limit Map with createFixedWindowRateLimiter(maxTrackedKeys=4096) at lines 46-50, and uses the bounded helpers at lines 117 and 164. Its regression test sends 200 unauthorized requests with different query nonces and asserts status-counter size 1; a separate authenticated churn test asserts rate limiting and state size 1. The same commit's CHANGELOG entry explicitly describes Zalo query-string normalization and bounded security tracking.

Version membership: git tag --contains reports a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3 first in normal release v2026.2.19 and 43cad8268d46a3663c79be831f2cacb015114882 first in v2026.3.1. git merge-base --is-ancestor succeeds for BIC -> v2026.2.19 and fix -> v2026.3.1, while fix -> v2026.2.26 exits 1, confirming v2026.2.26 remained vulnerable and the fix landed at the patched boundary.

BIC-only AI evidence: the raw commit object for a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3 has exactly one parent, human author/committer Peter Steinberger, and only the subject/body shown above with no AI attribution trailers. An all-ref exact-subject history search found only this commit object, so there was no reconstructable squash/member history to substitute for the direct one-parent BIC.
reasoning: The lifecycle begins in the one-parent hardening commit a23e0d5140e5126f5055a46824cae4ba0a097ba3: existing normalized-path route resolution was retained, but the commit added process-global security Maps and passed raw req.url to the pre-authentication 401 anomaly counter. Because URL query data is ignored for routing yet retained in the counter key, each unauthenticated query variant on the same valid path inserted a permanent distinct key. The immediate parent e0aaf2d399753e0a80d73409f30567394ee4a8b5 has neither the Map nor any status-recording/raw-URL key path, establishing direct parent absence. Subsequent commits 453664f09d0911cc1829d22c63f664f0ad2c8c10 and 3a68c56264bb42677c6bd38f487f3bc7d6c573bb are respectively a code move and later guardrail refactor, not introducers. Commit 43cad8268d46a3663c79be831f2cacb015114882 directly closes the advisory mechanism by keying on the matched pathname and bounding/pruning both security trackers, and its membership in v2026.3.1 matches the patched boundary while v2026.2.26 lacks it. Finally, the BIC commit object contains no AI marker and identifies a human author and committer, so under BIC-only attribution the closed verdict is NOT_AI regardless of any evidence outside that commit object.
